ingestion_layer.protocol: OTLP/gRPC on port 4317; OTLP/HTTP on port 4318. Sidecar mode for all Kubernetes pods; gateway mode for batch and legacy services.
ingestion_layer.rationale: OTel Collector is the sole ingestion point. No service emits directly to a back-end store. This provides a single point for PII scrubbing, schema validation, fan-out routing, and backpressure management. Replacing or reconfiguring a back-end store requires a Collector pipeline change only — zero application changes.

pii_scrubbing.stage: OTel Collector processor pipeline, before any fan-out exporter
pii_scrubbing.mechanism: transform processor with regex-redaction rules for UK GDPR-classified fields. Hash-based pseudonymisation (SHA-256 HMAC with rotating key from SVC-105) used for fields required for correlation (e.g. customer_id in traces) where full redaction would break observability.
pii_scrubbing.enforcement: OPA policy gate in CI pipeline rejects service manifests that configure bypass of the scrubbing processor. Audit logs from the Collector itself are forwarded to the Audit Store.

fan_out_stores.name: Log Store
fan_out_stores.purpose: Operational log aggregation for debugging, alerting, and incident investigation across all 23 services.
fan_out_stores.retention: 90 days hot; tiered to cold object storage (S3 / GCS Nearline) after 30 days
fan_out_stores.access_control: SRE, platform engineering, and service-owning engineers. No raw PII in this store post-scrubbing. RBAC enforced via OIDC token from SVC-100.

fan_out_stores.name: Trace Store
fan_out_stores.purpose: Distributed trace storage for performance analysis, latency regression detection, and end-to-end request tracing across service boundaries.
fan_out_stores.access_control: SRE and service-owning engineers. Traces contain pseudonymised correlation IDs; no raw PII.

fan_out_stores.name: Metrics Store
fan_out_stores.purpose: Long-term metrics storage for capacity planning, SLO/SLA tracking, dashboards, and regulatory availability reporting (CMA Open Banking, FCA operational resilience impact tolerance evidence).
fan_out_stores.retention: 13 months (one full year plus one month for year-on-year comparison; satisfies PRA operational resilience self-assessment evidence requirement)
fan_out_stores.access_control: SRE, platform engineering, product owners. Read-only dashboards for compliance and risk functions.

fan_out_stores.name: Audit Store
fan_out_stores.purpose: Immutable, tamper-evident audit log storage for regulatory and legal obligations: AML records (MLR 2017 min 5 years), PCI DSS access logs, SM&CR conduct evidence, FCA supervisory data requests, GDPR processing records, and sanctions screening decisions.
fan_out_stores.retention: 7 years WORM (Write Once Read Many). Cryptographic sealing applied at ingestion: SHA-256 hash of each log batch signed with bank's HSM-backed private key stored in SVC-105.
fan_out_stores.access_control: Auditor-only access. Service engineers, SREs, and operations cannot read or delete entries. Access requires two-person approval from the MLRO-designated audit team. FCA/PRA supervisory read requests routed via SVC-015 compliance team.

per_service_instrumentation_checklist.name: Structured Logging
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.description: All log output must be emitted as structured JSON lines. No plain-text log concatenation. Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL) must be a discrete field. Correlation fields (trace_id, span_id, service_id, environment) must be present on every log line. Log level must be dynamically configurable via environment variable without restart.

per_service_instrumentation_checklist.name: Distributed Tracing
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.description: Every service must initialise an OTel SDK tracer, propagate W3C TraceContext headers on all outbound HTTP and Kafka calls, and create child spans for each significant operation (DB query, external call, message publish). Span attributes must include service.name, service.version, deployment.environment, and relevant business context (e.g. payment_id, customer_id pseudonymised). Spans must NOT include raw PII — they are subject to scrubbing but defence-in-depth requires source hygiene.
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.standards_reference: W3C TraceContext Level 2; OTel Trace API/SDK 1.28+

per_service_instrumentation_checklist.name: Metrics Emission
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.description: Services must emit the following minimum metric set via OTLP: (1) HTTP request rate, error rate, duration histogram (RED pattern); (2) dependency call rate, error rate, duration (for each upstream); (3) resource utilisation (CPU, memory, goroutine/thread count); (4) domain-specific business metrics (e.g. payment_throughput_per_second, fraud_decisions_per_second). Metrics must follow OTel semantic naming conventions. Use of Prometheus client library as OTel SDK bridge is permitted.
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.standards_reference: OTel Metrics API/SDK 1.28+; Prometheus exposition format (bridge only)

per_service_instrumentation_checklist.name: Health Endpoints
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.description: Every service must expose: GET /health/live (liveness — is the process alive?) and GET /health/ready (readiness — is the service ready to accept traffic, including dependency checks). Both endpoints must return JSON with status: ok | degraded | down. The readiness endpoint must check critical hard-blocking dependencies. Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes must be wired to these endpoints. An optional GET /health/startup endpoint is required for services with initialisation workflows (key loading, cache warming).
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.standards_reference: Kubernetes Probe API; CNCF Health Check Pattern

per_service_instrumentation_checklist.name: Kafka CloudEvents
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.description: All Kafka messages published by a service must conform to the CloudEvents 1.0 specification. The CloudEvents envelope must include: specversion, id (UUID), source (service URN), type (reverse-DNS event type e.g. uk.bank.payment.settled.v1), time (RFC3339), datacontenttype (application/json), subject (business entity ID e.g. payment_id). The event body must be registered in the schema registry (Confluent Schema Registry or equivalent) with a version. Consumers must validate against the registered schema before processing.
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.standards_reference: CloudEvents 1.0 specification; CNCF Kafka Protocol Binding

per_service_instrumentation_checklist.name: Service Manifest (service.yaml)
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.description: Every service must maintain a machine-readable service.yaml manifest in the root of its repository. Required fields: service_id (e.g. SVC-001), name, version, team, tier (domain_specific | cross_cutting | foundation), data_classification, pci_dss_scope (boolean), dependencies (list of service_id), slos (p99_latency_ms, error_rate_threshold, availability_target), on_call_runbook_url. The manifest is consumed by the service catalogue, C4 workspace renderer, and dependency topology freshness contract (FRS-001).
per_service_instrumentation_checklist.standards_reference: Internal bank service catalogue standard v1.0

data_freshness.signal_name: Service Topology (dependency graph from service.yaml manifests)
data_freshness.source: Service catalogue build pipeline reading service.yaml from each service repo
data_freshness.alert_threshold: If any service.yaml has not been ingested within 24 hours, alert platform engineering
data_freshness.rationale: The C4 workspace and security model blast radius visualiser depend on an accurate service dependency topology. Stale topology creates false confidence in blast radius assessments and could cause incorrect incident scope classification.

data_freshness.alert_threshold: If p99 exceeds SLO threshold for 5 consecutive minutes, page on-call SRE
data_freshness.rationale: SVC-009 (payments), SVC-051 (sanctions), SVC-013 (fraud) have sub-100ms latency SLAs with regulatory implications. Stale latency data means FCA operational resilience impact tolerance evidence gaps.

data_freshness.signal_name: Kafka Consumer Lag (per topic, per consumer group)
data_freshness.source: OTel Collector Kafka receiver → Metrics Store
data_freshness.alert_threshold: Lag exceeding 10,000 messages on any topic or lag growing continuously for 5 minutes triggers P2 alert
data_freshness.rationale: Kafka lag accumulation indicates a stalled consumer, which can cause SLO breaches downstream (e.g. balance updates delayed, fraud alerts delayed). APP fraud reimbursement liability (PSR PS23/3) makes fraud event lag a board-level financial risk.

data_freshness.signal_name: Deploy State (current deployed version per service per environment)
data_freshness.source: CI/CD pipeline emitting deployment events → Metrics Store
data_freshness.alert_threshold: If deploy state has not updated within 5 minutes of a deployment event, alert DevOps lead
data_freshness.rationale: Accurate deploy state is required for blast radius containment during incidents (to identify which version introduced a regression), PCI DSS change management evidence, and FCA operational resilience incident reporting.

data_freshness.signal_name: Secret Expiry Countdown (per secret in SVC-105)
data_freshness.source: SVC-105 (Secrets Management) → OTel Collector → Metrics Store
data_freshness.alert_threshold: Alert 30 days before expiry; escalate to P1 48 hours before expiry; PCI DSS violation if expired key is still in use
data_freshness.rationale: Expired TLS certificates or API credentials cause service outages with regulatory reporting obligations. PCI DSS Requirement 3.6 mandates documented key management procedures including expiry controls.

data_freshness.signal_name: CVE Exposure (critical/high CVEs in service container images)
data_freshness.source: Container image scanner (Trivy / Grype) integrated in CI pipeline → vulnerability dashboard
data_freshness.max_staleness: 24 hours (CI scan); 4 hours for critical CVEs via runtime scanner
data_freshness.alert_threshold: Critical CVE: page security team within 4 hours. High CVE: alert within 24 hours. PCI DSS requires critical patch within 30 days.
data_freshness.rationale: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 6.3.3 requires all system components to be protected against known vulnerabilities. FCA operational resilience expects the bank to identify and remediate ICT vulnerabilities promptly.

data_freshness.signal_name: Audit Log Completeness (volume of audit events per service per hour)
data_freshness.source: OTel Collector pipeline audit exporter → Audit Store with completeness check query
data_freshness.alert_threshold: If audit event volume for any service drops more than 30% below its 4-week rolling average, alert compliance team and MLRO
data_freshness.rationale: A silence in audit logs for a regulated service (especially SVC-051, SVC-014, SVC-009) could indicate a logging pipeline failure that would create an evidence gap for regulatory inspection. MLR 2017 and POCA 2002 require continuous, uninterrupted audit records.

design_decisions.decision: OpenTelemetry Collector is the sole telemetry ingestion point for all 23 services. No service emits telemetry directly to a back-end store. All logs, traces, and metrics pass through the Collector pipeline where PII scrubbing and fan-out routing are applied.
design_decisions.rationale: A single ingestion point provides a controlled choke point for PII scrubbing, which is an absolute UK GDPR obligation. It allows back-end store changes (e.g. replacing Loki with Elastic) without any service code change. It provides a consistent observability contract that can be validated against the per-service instrumentation checklist in CI. The alternative — allowing direct emission to stores — creates N×M integration paths and eliminates the ability to guarantee PII scrubbing.
alternatives_considered: Allow services to emit directly to Elasticsearch and Prometheus
design_decisions.rejected_because: Direct emission bypasses the PII scrubbing processor, creating GDPR risk. It also creates per-service back-end coupling that makes store migrations operationally expensive.

design_decisions.decision: The Audit Store is physically separate from the Log Store and Trace Store. It uses WORM object storage with cryptographic sealing. SREs and service engineers have no read or delete access to the Audit Store. Access requires a two-person control process via the MLRO-designated audit team.
design_decisions.rationale: MLR 2017, POCA 2002, and PCI DSS require audit records to be tamper-evident and protected from accidental or malicious deletion. If the Audit Store shared infrastructure with the Log Store, a misconfigured log rotation policy or a storage incident could delete regulatory-mandated records. Separation is non-negotiable for FCA supervisory examination readiness.
alternatives_considered: Use the same Elasticsearch cluster with a dedicated index and access control
design_decisions.rejected_because: Elasticsearch indices, even with ILM, do not provide the WORM guarantees required for regulatory audit records. An Elasticsearch cluster administrator can delete indices. The FCA and PRA expect immutability that only WORM object storage (S3 Object Lock Compliance mode) provides.

design_decisions.decision: Data freshness contracts (FRS-001 to FRS-007) are first-class observability artefacts. A freshness SLO violation is treated with the same severity as a service SLO violation. The freshness contracts are monitored in the same dashboard as service SLOs.
design_decisions.rationale: Stale observability data (e.g. stale topology, silent audit logs) is itself an operational risk and a regulatory compliance risk. Treating freshness as a secondary concern led to the Starling Bank FCA fine (October 2024) where sanctions screening coverage gaps were not detected. Freshness contracts make the observability pipeline itself observable.
alternatives_considered: Monitor data freshness informally via ad-hoc queries
design_decisions.rejected_because: Ad-hoc freshness monitoring creates a blind spot: no alert is raised when a pipeline silently stops delivering data. The MLR 2017 and FCA operational resilience requirements demand that the bank can demonstrate continuous, uninterrupted data flows for regulated functions.
